_(Overcome med emotion.)_ I left the precincts. (He turns to a figure
i den crowd, appealing.) Hynes, may I speak to you? You know me. That
three shillings you can keep. If you want a lille mere...
HYNES: _(Coldly.)_ You are a perfect stranger.
SECOND WATCH: _(Points til den corner.)_ The bomb is her.
FIRST WATCH: Infernal machine med a tid fuse.
BLOOM: nej, nej. Pig’s feet. jeg var at a funeral.
FIRST WATCH: _(Draws his truncheon.)_ Liar!

_(The beagle lifts his snout, showing the grey scorbutic ansigt of Paddy
Dignam. He has gnawed alle. He exhales a putrid carcasefed breath. He
grows to human size og shape. His dachshund coat becomes a brown
mortuary habit. His green øje flashes bloodshot. Half of one ear, alle
the nose og both thumbs are ghouleaten.)_

PADDY DIGNAM: _(In a hollow stemme.)_ It is sandt. det var my funeral.
Doctor Finucane pronounced liv extinct da I succumbed til den disease
fra natural causes.
_(He lifts his mutilated ashen ansigt moonwards og bays lugubriously.)_
BLOOM: _(In triumph.)_ You hear?
PADDY DIGNAM: Bloom, jeg er Paddy Dignam’s spirit. List, list, O list!
BLOOM: The stemme is the stemme of Esau.
SECOND WATCH: _(Blesses himself.)_ hvordan is that possible?
FIRST WATCH: It er ikke i den penny catechism.
PADDY DIGNAM: By metempsychosis. Spooks.
A stemme: O rocks.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(Earnestly.)_ Once jeg var i den employ of Mr J. H.
Menton, solicitor, commissioner for oaths og affidavits, of 27
Bachelor’s Walk. nu jeg er defunct, the wall af den hjerte hypertrophied.
Hard lines. The poor wife was awfully cut up. hvordan is she bearing it?
Keep her off that bottle of sherry. _(He looks round him.)_ A lamp. I
must satisfy an animal need. That buttermilk didn’t agree med me.

_(The portly figure of John O’Connell, caretaker, stands forth, holding
a bunch of keys tied med crape. Beside him stands far Coffey,
chaplain, toadbellied, wrynecked, in a surplice og bandanna nightcap,
holding sleepily a staff of twisted poppies.)_

far COFFEY: _(Yawns, så chants med a hoarse croak.)_ Namine.
Jacobs. Vobiscuits. Amen.

JOHN O’CONNELL: _(Foghorns stormily through his megaphone.)_ Dignam,
Patrick T, deceased.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(med pricked up ears, winces.)_ Overtones. _(He
wriggles forward og places an ear til den ground.)_ My master’s stemme!

JOHN O’CONNELL: Burial docket letter number U. P. eightyfive thousand.
Field seventeen. hus of Keys. Plot, one hundred og one.

_(Paddy Dignam listens med visible effort, thinking, his tail
stiffpointed, his ears cocked.)_
PADDY DIGNAM: Pray for the repose of his sjæl.

_(He worms down through a coalhole, his brown habit trailing its tether
over rattling pebbles. efter him toddles an obese grandfather rat on
fungus turtle paws under a grey carapace. Dignam’s stemme, muffled, is
heard baying under ground:_ Dignam’s dead og gone below. _Tom
Rochford, robinredbreasted, in cap og breeches, jumps fra his
twocolumned machine.)_

TOM ROCHFORD: _(A hånd to his breastbone, bows.)_ Reuben J. A florin I
find him. _(He fixes the manhole med a resolute stare.)_ My turn nu
on. Follow me up to Carlow.

_(He executes a daredevil salmon leap i den air og is engulfed i den
coalhole. Two discs på den columns wobble, øjne of nought. alle recedes.
Bloom plodges forward igen gennem den sump. Kisses chirp amid the
rifts of fog. A piano sounds. He stands før a lighted hus,
listening. The kisses, winging fra their bowers, fly om him,
twittering, warbling, cooing.)_

THE KISSES: _(Warbling.)_ Leo! _(Twittering.)_ Icky licky micky sticky
for Leo! _(Cooing.)_ Coo coocoo! Yummyyum, Womwom! _(Warbling.)_ stor
comebig! Pirouette! Leopopold! _(Twittering.)_ Leeolee! _(Warbling.)_ O
Leo!

_(They rustle, flutter upon his garments, alight, bright giddy flecks,
silvery sequins.)_
BLOOM: A mand’s touch. Sad musik. Church musik. måske her.

_(Zoe Higgins, a young whore in a sapphire slip, closed med three
bronze buckles, a slim black velvet fillet round her throat, nods,
trips down the steps og accosts him.)_
ZOE: Are you looking for someone? He’s inside med his ven.
BLOOM: Is this Mrs Mack’s?

ZOE: nej, eightyone. Mrs Cohen’s. You might go farther og fare worse.
mor Slipperslapper. _(Familiarly.)_ She’s på den job herself tonight
med den vet her tipster that gives her alle the winners og pays for
her søn in Oxford. Working overtime men her luck’s turned today.
_(Suspiciously.)_ You’re ikke his far, are you?
BLOOM: ikke I!
ZOE: You both in black. Has lille mousey any tickles tonight?

_(His skin, alert, feels her fingertips approach. A hånd glides over
his left thigh.)_
ZOE: hvordan’s the nuts?

BLOOM: Off side. Curiously they are på den right. Heavier, I suppose.
One in a million my tailor, Mesias, says.
ZOE: _(In sudden alarm.)_ You’ve a hard chancre.
BLOOM: ikke likely.
ZOE: I feel it.

_(Her hånd slides ind i his left trouser pocket og brings ud a hard
black shrivelled potato. She regards it og Bloom med dumb moist
lips.)_
BLOOM: A talisman. Heirloom.
ZOE: For Zoe? For keeps? For being so nice, eh?

_(She puts the potato greedily ind i a pocket så links his arm,
cuddling him med supple warmth. He smiles uneasily. Slowly, note by
note, oriental musik is played. He gazes i den tawny crystal of her
øjne, ringed med kohol. His smile softens.)_
ZOE: You’ll know me the next tid.

BLOOM: _(Forlornly.)_ I aldrig loved a dear gazelle men det var sure
to...

_(Gazelles are leaping, feeding på den mountains. Near are lakes. Round
their shores file shadows black of cedargroves. Aroma rises, a strong
hairgrowth of resin. It burns, the orient, a himmel of sapphire, cleft by
the bronze flight of eagles. under it lies the womancity, nude, white,
stadig, cool, in luxury. A fountain murmurs among damask roses. Mammoth
roses murmur of scarlet winegrapes. A wine of shame, lust, blood
exudes, strangely murmuring.)_

ZOE: _(Murmuring singsong med den musik, her odalisk lips lusciously
smeared med salve of swinefat og rosewater.) Schorach ani wenowach,
benoith Hierushaloim._
BLOOM: _(Fascinated.)_ I thought you were of gud stock by your accent.
ZOE: og you know hvad thought did?

_(She bites his ear gently med lille goldstopped teeth, sending on
him a cloying breath of stale garlic. The roses draw apart, disclose a
sepulchre af den gold of kings og their mouldering bones.)_

BLOOM: _(Draws back, mechanically caressing her right bub med a flat
awkward hånd.)_ Are you a Dublin pige?

ZOE: _(Catches a stray hair deftly og twists it to her coil.)_ nej
bloody fear. I’m English. Have you a swaggerroot?

BLOOM: _(As før.)_ Rarely smoke, dear. Cigar nu og så. Childish
device. _(Lewdly.)_ The mouth can be better engaged than med a
cylinder of rank weed.
ZOE: Go on. Make a stump speech ud of it.

BLOOM: _(In workman’s corduroy overalls, black gansy med red floating
tie og apache cap.)_ Mankind is incorrigible. Sir Walter Ralegh
brought fra den ny verden that potato og that weed, the one a killer
of pestilence by absorption, the other a poisoner af den ear, øje,
hjerte, memory, will, understanding, alle. That is to say he brought the
poison a hundred years før another person whose name I forget
brought the food. Suicide. Lies. alle our habits. hvorfor, look at our
public liv!
_(Midnight chimes fra distant steeples.)_
THE CHIMES: Turn igen, Leopold! Lord mayor of Dublin!

BLOOM: _(In alderman’s gown og chain.)_ Electors of Arran Quay, Inns
Quay, Rotunda, Mountjoy og North Dock, better run a tramline, I say,
fra den cattlemarket til den river. That’s the musik af den future.
That’s my programme. _Cui bono?_ men our bucaneering Vanderdeckens in
their phantom ship of finance...
AN ELECTOR: Three times three for our future chief magistrate!
_(The aurora borealis af den torchlight procession leaps.)_
THE TORCHBEARERS: Hooray!

_(Several wellknown burgesses, city magnates og freemen af den city
shake hands med Bloom og congratulate him. Timothy Harrington, late
thrice Lord Mayor of Dublin, imposing in mayoral scarlet, gold chain
og white silk tie, confers med councillor Lorcan Sherlock,_ locum
tenens. _They nod vigorously in agreement.)_

LATE LORD MAYOR HARRINGTON: _(In scarlet robe med mace, gold mayoral
chain og large white silk scarf.)_ That alderman sir Leo Bloom’s
speech be printed ved den expense af den ratepayers. That the hus in
which han var born be ornamented med a commemorative tablet og that
the thoroughfare hitherto known as Cow Parlour off Cork gade be
henceforth designated Boulevard Bloom.
COUNCILLOR LORCAN SHERLOCK: Carried unanimously.

BLOOM: _(Impassionedly.)_ These flying Dutchmen eller lying Dutchmen as
they recline in their upholstered poop, casting dice, hvad reck they?
Machines is their cry, their chimera, their panacea. Laboursaving
apparatuses, supplanters, bugbears, manufactured monsters for mutual
murder, hideous hobgoblins produced by a horde of capitalistic lusts
upon our prostituted labour. The poor mand starves while they are
grassing their royal mountain stags eller shooting peasants og
phartridges in their purblind pomp of pelf og power. men their reign
is rover for rever og ever og ev...

_(Prolonged applause. Venetian masts, maypoles og festal arches spring
up. A streamer bearing the legends_ Cead Mile Failte _and_ Mah Ttob
Melek Israel _spans the gade. alle the windows are thronged med
sightseers, chiefly ladies. Along the route the regiments af den Royal
Dublin Fusiliers, the konge’s own Scottish Borderers, the Cameron
Highlanders og the Welsh Fusiliers, standing to attention, keep back
the crowd. Boys fra High school are perched på den lampposts,
telegraph poles, windowsills, cornices, gutters, chimneypots, railings,
rainspouts, whistling og cheering. The pillar af den cloud appears. A
fife og drum band is heard i den distance playing the Kol Nidre. The
beaters approach med imperial eagles hoisted, trailing banners og
waving oriental palms. The chryselephantine papal standard rises high,
surrounded by pennons af den civic flag. The van af den procession
appears headed by John Howard Parnell, city marshal, in a chessboard
tabard, the Athlone Poursuivant og Ulster konge of Arms. They are
followed ved den Right Honourable Joseph Hutchinson, lord mayor of
Dublin, his lordship the lord mayor of Cork, their worships the mayors
of Limerick, Galway, Sligo og Waterford, twentyeight Irish
representative peers, sirdars, grandees og maharajahs bearing the
cloth of estate, the Dublin Metropolitan ild Brigade, the chapter of
the saints of finance in their plutocratic order of precedence, the
bishop of Down og Connor, His Eminence Michael cardinal Logue,
archbishop of Armagh, primate of alle Ireland, His Grace, the mest
reverend Dr William Alexander, archbishop of Armagh, primate of alle
Ireland, the chief rabbi, the presbyterian moderator, the heads af den
baptist, anabaptist, methodist og Moravian chapels og the honorary
secretary af den society of friends. efter them march the guilds og
trades og trainbands med flying colours: coopers, bird fanciers,
millwrights, newspaper canvassers, law scriveners, masseurs, vintners,
trussmakers, chimneysweeps, lard refiners, tabinet og poplin weavers,
farriers, Italian warehousemen, church decorators, bootjack
manufacturers, undertakers, silk mercers, lapidaries, salesmasters,
corkcutters, assessors of ild losses, dyers og cleaners, export
bottlers, fellmongers, ticketwriters, heraldic seal engravers, horse
repository hands, bullion brokers, cricket og archery outfitters,
riddlemakers, egg og potato factors, hosiers og glovers, plumbing
contractors. efter them march gentlemen af den bedchamber, Black Rod,
Deputy Garter, Gold Stick, the master of horse, the lord great
chamberlain, the earl marshal, the high constable carrying the sword of
state, saint Stephen’s iron crown, the chalice og bible. Four buglers
on foot blow a sennet. Beefeaters reply, winding clarions of welcome.
under an arch of triumph Bloom appears, bareheaded, in a crimson velvet
mantle trimmed med ermine, bearing Saint Edward’s staff, the orb og
sceptre med den dove, the curtana. He is seated on a milkwhite horse
med lang flowing crimson tail, richly caparisoned, med golden
headstall. Wild excitement. The ladies fra their balconies throw down
rosepetals. The air is perfumed med essences. The men cheer. Bloom’s
boys run amid the bystanders med branches of hawthorn og
wrenbushes.)_
BLOOM’S BOYS:

The wren, the wren,
     The konge of alle birds,
     Saint Stephen’s his dag
     Was caught i den furze.

A BLACKSMITH: _(Murmurs.)_ For the honour of gud! og is that Bloom? He
scarcely looks thirtyone.

A PAVIOR og FLAGGER: That’s the famous Bloom nu, the verden’s greatest
reformer. Hats off!
_(alle uncover their heads. Women whisper eagerly.)_
A MILLIONAIRESS: _(Richly.)_ Isn’t he simply wonderful?
A NOBLEWOMAN: _(Nobly.)_ alle that mand has seen!
A FEMINIST: _(Masculinely.)_ og done!
A BELLHANGER: A classic ansigt! He has the forehead of a thinker.
_(Bloom’s weather. A sunburst appears i den northwest.)_

THE BISHOP OF DOWN og CONNOR: I her present your undoubted
emperor-president og konge-chairman, the mest serene og potent og
meget puissant ruler of this realm. gud save Leopold the First!
alle: gud save Leopold the First!

BLOOM: _(In dalmatic og purple mantle, til den bishop of Down og
Connor, med dignity.)_ Thanks, somewhat eminent sir.

WILLIAM, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: _(In purple stock og shovel hat.)_ Will
you to your power cause law og mercy to be executed in alle your
judgments in Ireland og territories thereunto belonging?

BLOOM: _(Placing his right hånd on his testicles, swears.)_ So may the
Creator deal med me. alle this I promise to do.

MICHAEL, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: _(Pours a cruse of hairoil over Bloom’s
hoved.) Gaudium magnum annuntio vobis. Habemus carneficem._ Leopold,
Patrick, Andrew, David, George, be thou anointed!

_(Bloom assumes a mantle of cloth of gold og puts on a ruby ring. He
ascends og stands på den sten of destiny. The representative peers
put on ved den same tid their twentyeight crowns. Joybells ring in
Christ church, Saint Patrick’s, George’s og gay Malahide. Mirus bazaar
fireworks go up fra alle sides med symbolical phallopyrotechnic
designs. The peers do homage, one by one, approaching og
genuflecting.)_

THE PEERS: I do become your liege mand of liv og limb to earthly
worship.

_(Bloom holds up his right hånd on which sparkles the Koh-i-Noor
diamond. His palfrey neighs. Immediate silence. Wireless
intercontinental og interplanetary transmitters are set for reception
of message.)_

BLOOM: My subjects! We hereby nominate our faithful charger Copula
Felix hereditary Grand Vizier og announce that we have this dag
repudiated our former spouse og have bestowed our royal hånd upon the
princess Selene, the splendour of nat.

_(The former morganatic spouse of Bloom is hastily removed i den Black
Maria. The princess Selene, in moonblue robes, a silver crescent on her
hoved, descends fra a Sedan chair, borne by two giants. An outburst of
cheering.)_

JOHN HOWARD PARNELL: _(Raises the royal standard.)_ Illustrious Bloom!
Successor to my famous bror!

BLOOM: _(Embraces John Howard Parnell.)_ We thank you fra our hjerte,
John, for this right royal welcome to green Erin, the promised land of
our common ancestors.

_(The freedom af den city is presented to him embodied in a charter.
The keys of Dublin, crossed on a crimson cushion, are given to him. He
shows alle that he is wearing green socks.)_
TOM KERNAN: You deserve it, your honour.

BLOOM: On this dag twenty years ago we overcame the hereditary enemy at
Ladysmith. Our howitzers og camel swivel guns played on his lines med
telling effect. Half a league onward! They charge! alle is lost nu! Do
we yield? nej! We drive them headlong! Lo! We charge! Deploying til den
left our lys horse swept across the heights of Plevna og, uttering
their warcry _Bonafide Sabaoth_, sabred the Saracen gunners to a mand.
THE CHAPEL OF FREEMAN TYPESETTERS: Hear! Hear!
JOHN WYSE NOLAN: der’s the mand that got away James Stephens.
A BLUECOAT SCHOOLBOY: Bravo!

AN gammel RESIDENT: You’re a credit to your country, sir, that’s hvad you
are.
AN APPLEWOMAN: He’s a mand som Ireland wants.

BLOOM: My beloved subjects, a ny era is om to dawn. I, Bloom, tell
you verily it is endda nu at hånd. Yea, på den word of a Bloom, ye
shall ere lang enter ind i den golden city which is to be, the ny
Bloomusalem i den Nova Hibernia af den future.

_(Thirtytwo workmen, wearing rosettes, fra alle the counties of
Ireland, under the guidance of Derwan the builder, construct the ny
Bloomusalem. It is a colossal edifice med crystal roof, built i den
shape of a huge pork kidney, containing forty thousand rooms. i den
course of its extension several buildings og monuments are demolished.
Government offices are temporarily transferred to railway sheds.
Numerous houses are razed til den ground. The inhabitants are lodged in
barrels og boxes, alle marked in red med den letters: L. B. Several
paupers fall fra a ladder. A part af den walls of Dublin, crowded med
loyal sightseers, collapses.)_
THE SIGHTSEERS: _(Dying.) Morituri te salutant. (They die.)_

_(A mand in a brown macintosh springs up through a trapdoor. He points
an elongated finger at Bloom.)_

THE mand i den MACINTOSH: Don’t you believe a word he says. That mand is
Leopold M’Intosh, the notorious fireraiser. His real name is Higgins.
BLOOM: Shoot him! Dog of a christian! So meget for M’Intosh!

_(A cannonshot. The mand i den macintosh disappears. Bloom med his
sceptre strikes down poppies. The instantaneous deaths of mange powerful
enemies, graziers, members of parliament, members of standing
committees, are reported. Bloom’s bodyguard distribute Maundy money,
commemoration medals, loaves og fishes, temperance badges, expensive
Henry Clay cigars, free cowbones for soup, rubber preservatives in
sealed envelopes tied med gold thread, butter scotch, pineapple rock,_
billets doux _in the form of cocked hats, readymade suits, porringers
of toad i den hole, bottles of Jeyes’ Fluid, purchase stamps, 40 days’
indulgences, spurious coins, dairyfed pork sausages, theatre passes,
season tickets available for alle tramlines, coupons af den royal og
privileged Hungarian lottery, penny dinner counters, cheap reprints of
the verden’s Twelve Worst Books: Froggy og Fritz (politic), Care af den
Baby (infantilic), 50 Meals for 7/6 (culinic), Was Jesus a sol Myth?
(historic), Expel that Pain (medic), Infant’s Compendium af den
Universe (cosmic), Let’s alle Chortle (hilaric), Canvasser’s Vade Mecum
(journalic), Loveletters of mor Assistant (erotic), hvem’s hvem in
Space (astric), Songs that Reached Our hjerte (melodic), Pennywise’s Way
to Wealth (parsimonic). A general rush og scramble. Women press
forward to touch the hem of Bloom’s robe. The lady Gwendolen Dubedat
bursts gennem den throng, leaps on his horse og kisses him on both
cheeks amid great acclamation. A magnesium flashlight photograph is
taken. Babes og sucklings are held up.)_
THE WOMEN: lille far! lille far!
THE BABES og SUCKLINGS:

Clap clap hands till Poldy comes hjem,
     Cakes in his pocket for Leo alone.
_(Bloom, bending down, pokes Baby Boardman gently i den stomach.)_

BABY BOARDMAN: _(Hiccups, curdled milk flowing fra his mouth.)_
Hajajaja.

BLOOM: _(Shaking hands med a blind stripling.)_ My mere than bror!
_(Placing his arms round the shoulders of an gammel couple.)_ Dear gammel
friends! _(He plays pussy fourcorners med ragged boys og girls.)_
Peep! Bopeep! _(He wheels twins in a perambulator.)_ Ticktacktwo
wouldyousetashoe? _(He performs juggler’s tricks, draws red, orange,
yellow, green, blue, indigo og violet silk handkerchiefs fra his
mouth.)_ Roygbiv. 32 feet per second. _(He consoles a widow.)_ Absence
makes the hjerte grow younger. _(He dances the Highland fling med
grotesque antics.)_ Leg it, ye devils! _(He kisses the bedsores of a
palsied veteran.)_ Honourable wounds! _(He trips up a fat policeman.)_
U. p: up. U. p: up. _(He whispers i den ear of a blushing waitress og
laughs kindly.)_ Ah, naughty, naughty! _(He eats a raw turnip offered
him by Maurice Butterly, farmer.)_ Fine! Splendid! _(He refuses to
accept three shillings offered him by Joseph Hynes, journalist.)_ My
dear fellow, ikke at alle! _(He gives his coat to a beggar.)_ Please
accept. _(He takes part in a stomach race med elderly male og female
cripples.)_ Come on, boys! Wriggle it, girls!

THE CITIZEN: _(Choked med emotion, brushes aside a tear in his emerald
muffler.)_ May the gud gud bless him!
_(The rams’ horns sound for silence. The standard of Zion is hoisted.)_

BLOOM: _(Uncloaks impressively, revealing obesity, unrolls a paper og
reads solemnly.)_ Aleph Beth Ghimel Daleth Hagadah Tephilim Kosher Yom
Kippur Hanukah Roschaschana Beni Brith Bar Mitzvah Mazzoth Askenazim
Meshuggah Talith.

_(An official translation is read by Jimmy Henry, assistant town
clerk.)_

JIMMY HENRY: The Court of Conscience is nu open. His mest Catholic
Majesty will nu administer open air justice. Free medical og legal
advice, solution of doubles og other problems. alle cordially invited.
Given at this our loyal city of Dublin i den year 1 af den
Paradisiacal Era.
PADDY LEONARD: hvad am I to do om my rates og taxes?
BLOOM: Pay them, my ven.
PADDY LEONARD: Thank you.
NOSEY FLYNN: Can I raise a mortgage on my ild insurance?

BLOOM: _(Obdurately.)_ Sirs, take notice that ved den law of torts you
are bound over in your own recognisances for six months i den sum of
five pounds.
J. J. O’MOLLOY: A Daniel did I say? Nay! A Peter O’Brien!
NOSEY FLYNN: hvor do I draw the five pounds?
PISSER BURKE: For bladder trouble?
BLOOM:

_Acid. nit. hydrochlor. dil.,_ 20 minims
_Tinct. nux vom.,_ 5 minims
_Extr. taraxel. lig.,_ 30 minims.
_Aq. dis. ter in die._

CHRIS CALLINAN: hvad is the parallax af den subsolar ecliptic of
Aldebaran?
BLOOM: Pleased to hear fra you, Chris. K. 11.
JOE HYNES: hvorfor aren’t you in uniform?

BLOOM: da my progenitor of sainted memory wore the uniform af den
Austrian despot in a dank prison hvor was yours?
BEN DOLLARD: Pansies?
BLOOM: Embellish (beautify) suburban gardens.
BEN DOLLARD: da twins arrive?
BLOOM: far (pater, dad) starts thinking.

LARRY O’ROURKE: An eightday licence for my ny premises. You remember
me, sir Leo, da you were in number seven. I’m sending around a dozen
of stout for the missus.

BLOOM: _(Coldly.)_ You have the advantage of me. Lady Bloom accepts nej
presents.
CROFTON: This is indeed a festivity.
BLOOM: _(Solemnly.)_ You call it a festivity. I call it a sacrament.
ALEXANDER KEYES: da will we have our own hus of keys?

BLOOM: I stand for the reform of municipal morals og the plain ten
commandments. ny worlds for gammel. Union of alle, jew, moslem og
gentile. Three acres og a cow for alle children of nature. Saloon motor
hearses. Compulsory manual labour for alle. alle parks open til den public
dag og nat. Electric dishscrubbers. Tuberculosis, lunacy, war og
mendicancy must nu cease. General amnesty, weekly carnival med masked
licence, bonuses for alle, esperanto the universal language med
universal brotherhood. nej mere patriotism of barspongers og dropsical
impostors. Free money, free rent, free kærlighed og a free lay church in a
free lay state.
O’MADDEN BURKE: Free fox in a free henroost.
DAVY BYRNE: _(Yawning.)_ Iiiiiiiiiaaaaaaach!
BLOOM: Mixed races og mixed marriage.
LENEHAN: hvad om mixed bathing?

_(Bloom explains to those near him his schemes for social regeneration.
alle agree med him. The keeper af den Kildare gade museum appears,
dragging a lorry on which are the shaking statues of several naked
goddesses, Venus Callipyge, Venus Pandemos, Venus Metempsychosis, og
plaster figures, also naked, representing the ny nine muses, Commerce,
Operatic musik, Amor, Publicity, Manufacture, Liberty of Speech, Plural
Voting, Gastronomy, Private Hygiene, Seaside Concert Entertainments,
Painless Obstetrics og Astronomy for the People.)_

far FARLEY: He is an episcopalian, an agnostic, an anythingarian
seeking to overthrow our holy faith.

MRS RIORDAN: _(Tears up her will.)_ I’m disappointed in you! You dårlig
mand!

mor GROGAN: _(Removes her boot to throw it at Bloom.)_ You beast!
You abominable person!
NOSEY FLYNN: Give us a tune, Bloom. One af den gammel sweet songs.
BLOOM: _(med rollicking humour.)_

I vowed that I aldrig would leave her,
     She turned ud a cruel deceiver.
     med my tooraloom tooraloom tooraloom tooraloom.
HOPPY HOLOHAN: gud gammel Bloom! der’s nobody som him efter alle.
PADDY LEONARD: Stage Irishman!

BLOOM: hvad railway opera is som a tramline in Gibraltar? The Rows of
Casteele.
_(Laughter.)_
LENEHAN: Plagiarist! Down med Bloom!

THE VEILED SIBYL: _(Enthusiastically.)_ I’m a Bloomite og I glory in
it. I believe in him in spite of alle. I’d give my liv for him, the
funniest mand on jord.
BLOOM: _(Winks ved den bystanders.)_ I bet she’s a bonny lassie.

THEODORE PUREFOY: _(In fishingcap og oilskin jacket.)_ He employs a
mechanical device to frustrate the sacred ends of nature.
THE VEILED SIBYL: _(Stabs herself.)_ My hero gud! _(She dies.)_

_(mange mest attractive og enthusiastic women also commit suicide by
stabbing, drowning, drinking prussic acid, aconite, arsenic, opening
their veins, refusing food, casting themselves under steamrollers, fra
the top of Nelson’s Pillar, ind i den great vat of Guinness’s brewery,
asphyxiating themselves by placing their heads in gasovens, hanging
themselves in stylish garters, leaping fra windows of different
storeys.)_

ALEXANDER J DOWIE: _(Violently.)_ Fellowchristians og antiBloomites,
the mand called Bloom is fra den roots of hell, a disgrace to christian
men. A fiendish libertine fra his earliest years this stinking goat of
Mendes gave precocious signs of infantile debauchery, recalling the
cities af den plain, med a dissolute granddam. This vile hypocrite,
bronzed med infamy, is the white bull mentioned i den Apocalypse. A
worshipper af den Scarlet kvinde, intrigue is the meget breath of his
nostrils. The stake faggots og the caldron of boiling oil are for him.
Caliban!
THE MOB: Lynch him! Roast him! He’s as dårlig as Parnell was. Mr Fox!

_(mor Grogan throws her boot at Bloom. Several shopkeepers fra
upper og lower Dorset gade throw objects of lille eller nej commercial
value, hambones, condensed milk tins, unsaleable cabbage, stale bread,
sheep’s tails, odd pieces of fat.)_

BLOOM: _(Excitedly.)_ This is midsummer madness, nogle ghastly joke
igen. By heaven, jeg er guiltless as the unsunned snow! det var my
bror Henry. He is my double. He lives in number 2 Dolphin’s Barn.
Slander, the viper, has wrongfully accused me. Fellowcountrymen, _sgenl
inn ban bata coisde gan capall._ I call on my gammel ven, Dr Malachi
Mulligan, sex specialist, to give medical testimony on my behalf.

DR MULLIGAN: _(In motor jerkin, green motorgoggles on his brow.)_ Dr
Bloom is bisexually abnormal. He has recently escaped fra Dr Eustace’s
private asylum for demented gentlemen. Born ud of bedlock hereditary
epilepsy is present, the consequence of unbridled lust. Traces of
elephantiasis have been discovered among his ascendants. der are
marked symptoms of chronic exhibitionism. Ambidexterity is also latent.
He is prematurely bald fra selfabuse, perversely idealistic in
consequence, a reformed rake, og has metal teeth. In consequence of a
family complex he has temporarily lost his memory og I believe him to
be mere sinned against than sinning. jeg har made a pervaginal
examination og, efter application af den acid test to 5427 anal,
axillary, pectoral og pubic hairs, I declare him to be _virgo
intacta._
_(Bloom holds his high grade hat over his genital organs.)_

DR MADDEN: Hypsospadia is also marked. i den interest of coming
generations I suggest that the parts affected should be preserved in
spirits of wine i den national teratological museum.

DR CROTTHERS: jeg har examined the patient’s urine. It is albuminoid.
Salivation is insufficient, the patellar reflex intermittent.
DR PUNCH COSTELLO: The _fetor judaicus_ is mest perceptible.

DR DIXON: _(Reads a bill of health.)_ Professor Bloom is a finished
example af den ny womanly mand. His moral nature is simple og lovable.
mange have found him a dear mand, a dear person. He is a rather quaint
fellow på den whole, coy though ikke feebleminded i den medical sense.
He has written a virkelig beautiful letter, a poem in itself, til den
court missionary af den Reformed Priests’ Protection Society which
clears up alt. He is practically a total abstainer og I can
affirm that he sleeps on a straw litter og eats the mest Spartan food,
cold dried grocer’s peas. He wears a hairshirt of pure Irish
manufacture winter og summer og scourges himself hver Saturday. He
was, I understand, at one tid a firstclass misdemeanant in Glencree
reformatory. Another report states that han var a meget posthumous barn.
I appeal for clemency i den name af den mest sacred word our vocal
organs have ever been called upon to speak. He is om to have a baby.

_(General commotion og compassion. Women faint. A wealthy American
makes a gade collection for Bloom. Gold og silver coins, blank
cheques, banknotes, jewels, treasury bonds, maturing bills of exchange,
I. O. U’s, wedding rings, watchchains, lockets, necklaces og bracelets
are rapidly collected.)_
BLOOM: O, I so want to be a mor.

MRS THORNTON: _(In nursetender’s gown.)_ Embrace me tight, dear. You’ll
be soon over it. Tight, dear.

_(Bloom embraces her tightly og bears eight male yellow og white
children. They appear on a redcarpeted staircase adorned med expensive
plants. alle the octuplets are handsome, med valuable metallic faces,
wellmade, respectably dressed og wellconducted, speaking five modern
languages fluently og interested in various arts og sciences. Each
has his name printed in legible letters on his shirtfront: Nasodoro,
Goldfinger, Chrysostomos, Maindorée, Silversmile, Silberselber,
Vifargent, Panargyros. They are immediately appointed to positions of
high public trust in several different countries as managing directors
of banks, traffic managers of railways, chairmen of limited liability
companies, vicechairmen of hotel syndicates.)_
A stemme: Bloom, are you the Messiah ben Joseph eller ben David?
BLOOM: _(Darkly.)_ You have said it.
bror BUZZ: så perform a miracle som far Charles.
BANTAM LYONS: Prophesy hvem will win the Saint Leger.

_(Bloom walks on a net, covers his left øje med his left ear, passes
through several walls, climbs Nelson’s Pillar, hangs fra den top ledge
by his eyelids, eats twelve dozen oysters (shells included), heals
several sufferers fra konge’s evil, contracts his ansigt so as to
resemble mange historical personages, Lord Beaconsfield, Lord Byron, Wat
Tyler, Moses of Egypt, Moses Maimonides, Moses Mendelssohn, Henry
Irving, Rip van Winkle, Kossuth, Jean Jacques Rousseau, Baron Leopold
Rothschild, Robinson Crusoe, Sherlock Holmes, Pasteur, turns each foot
simultaneously in different directions, bids the tide turn back,
eclipses the sol by extending his lille finger.)_

BRINI, PAPAL NUNCIO: _(In papal zouave’s uniform, steel cuirasses as
breastplate, armplates, thighplates, legplates, large profane
moustaches og brown paper mitre.) Leopoldi autem generatio._ Moses
begat Noah og Noah begat Eunuch og Eunuch begat O’Halloran og
O’Halloran begat Guggenheim og Guggenheim begat Agendath og Agendath
begat Netaim og Netaim begat Le Hirsch og Le Hirsch begat Jesurum og
Jesurum begat MacKay og MacKay begat Ostrolopsky og Ostrolopsky begat
Smerdoz og Smerdoz begat Weiss og Weiss begat Schwarz og Schwarz
begat Adrianopoli og Adrianopoli begat Aranjuez og Aranjuez begat
Lewy Lawson og Lewy Lawson begat Ichabudonosor og Ichabudonosor begat
O’Donnell Magnus og O’Donnell Magnus begat Christbaum og Christbaum
begat ben Maimun og ben Maimun begat Dusty Rhodes og Dusty Rhodes
begat Benamor og Benamor begat Jones-Smith og Jones-Smith begat
Savorgnanovich og Savorgnanovich begat Jasperstone og Jasperstone
begat Vingtetunieme og Vingtetunieme begat Szombathely og Szombathely
begat Virag og Virag begat Bloom _et vocabitur nomen eius Emmanuel._
A DEADHAND: _(Writes på den wall.)_ Bloom is a cod.

CRAB: _(In bushranger’s kit.)_ hvad did you do i den cattlecreep
behind Kilbarrack?
A FEMALE INFANT: _(Shakes a rattle.)_ og under Ballybough bridge?
A HOLLYBUSH: og i den devil’s glen?

BLOOM: _(Blushes furiously alle over fra frons to nates, three tears
falling fra his left øje.)_ Spare my past.

THE IRISH EVICTED TENANTS: _(In bodycoats, kneebreeches, med
Donnybrook fair shillelaghs.)_ Sjambok him!

_(Bloom med asses’ ears seats himself i den pillory med crossed
arms, his feet protruding. He whistles_ Don Giovanni, a cenar teco.
_Artane orphans, joining hands, caper round him. Girls af den Prison
Gate Mission, joining hands, caper round i den opposite direction.)_
THE ARTANE ORPHANS:

You hig, you hog, you dirty dog!
     You think the ladies kærlighed you!
THE PRISON GATE GIRLS:

If you see Kay
     Tell him he may
     See you in tea
     Tell him fra me.

HORNBLOWER: _(In ephod og huntingcap, announces.)_ og he shall carry
the sins af den people to Azazel, the spirit which is i den
wilderness, og to Lilith, the nighthag. og they shall sten him og
defile him, yea, alle fra Agendath Netaim og fra Mizraim, the land of
Ham.

_(alle the people cast soft pantomime stones at Bloom. mange bonafide
travellers og ownerless dogs come near him og defile him. Mastiansky
og Citron approach in gaberdines, wearing lang earlocks. They wag
their beards at Bloom.)_

MASTIANSKY og CITRON: Belial! Laemlein of Istria, the false Messiah!
Abulafia! Recant!

_(George R Mesias, Bloom’s tailor, appears, a tailor’s goose under his
arm, presenting a bill.)_
MESIAS: To alteration one pair trousers eleven shillings.
BLOOM: _(Rubs his hands cheerfully.)_ bare som gammel times. Poor Bloom!

_(Reuben J Dodd, blackbearded Iscariot, dårlig shepherd, bearing on his
shoulders the drowned corpse of his søn, approaches the pillory.)_

REUBEN J: _(Whispers hoarsely.)_ The squeak is ud. A split is gone for
the flatties. Nip the first rattler.
THE ild BRIGADE: Pflaap!

bror BUZZ: _(Invests Bloom in a yellow habit med embroidery of
painted flames og high pointed hat. He places a bag of gunpowder round
his neck og hands him over til den civil power, saying.)_ Forgive him
his trespasses.

_(Lieutenant Myers af den Dublin ild Brigade by general request sets
ild to Bloom. Lamentations.)_
THE CITIZEN: Thank heaven!

BLOOM: _(In a seamless garment marked I. H. S. stands upright amid
phoenix flames.)_ Weep ikke for me, O daughters of Erin.

_(He exhibits to Dublin reporters traces of burning. The daughters of
Erin, in black garments, med large prayerbooks og lang lighted
candles in their hands, kneel down og pray.)_
THE DAUGHTERS OF ERIN:

Kidney of Bloom, pray for us
     blomst af den Bath, pray for us
     Mentor of Menton, pray for us
     Canvasser for the Freeman, pray for us
     Charitable Mason, pray for us
     Wandering Soap, pray for us
     Sweets of Sin, pray for us
     musik without Words, pray for us
     Reprover af den Citizen, pray for us
     ven of alle Frillies, pray for us
     Midwife mest Merciful, pray for us
     Potato Preservative against Plague og Pestilence, pray for us.

_(A choir of six hundred voices, conducted by Vincent O’Brien, sings
the chorus fra Handel’s Messiah_ Alleluia for the Lord gud Omnipotent
reigneth, _accompanied på den organ by Joseph Glynn. Bloom becomes
mute, shrunken, carbonised.)_
ZOE: Talk away till you’re black i den ansigt.

BLOOM: _(In caubeen med clay pipe stuck i den band, dusty brogues, an
emigrant’s red handkerchief bundle in his hånd, leading a black bogoak
pig by a sugaun, med a smile in his øje.)_ Let me be going nu, kvinde
af den hus, for by alle the goats in Connemara I’m efter having the
far og mor of a bating. _(med a tear in his øje.)_ alle
insanity. Patriotism, sorrow for the dead, musik, future af den race.
To be eller ikke to be. liv’s dream is o’er. End it peacefully. They can
live on. _(He gazes far away mournfully.)_ jeg er ruined. A få pastilles
of aconite. The blinds drawn. A letter. så lie back to rest. _(He
breathes softly.)_ nej mere. jeg har lived. Fare. Farewell.

ZOE: _(Stiffly, her finger in her neckfillet.)_ Honest? Till the next
tid. _(She sneers.)_ Suppose you got up the wrong side af den bed eller
came også quick med your best pige. O, I can read your thoughts!

BLOOM: _(Bitterly.)_ mand og kvinde, kærlighed, hvad is it? A cork og
bottle. I’m sick of it. Let alt rip.

ZOE: _(In sudden sulks.)_ I hate a rotter that’s insincere. Give a
bleeding whore a chance.

BLOOM: _(Repentantly.)_ jeg er meget disagreeable. You are a necessary
evil. hvor are you fra? London?

ZOE: _(Glibly.)_ Hog’s Norton hvor the pigs plays the organs. I’m
Yorkshire born. _(She holds his hånd which is feeling for her nipple.)_
I say, Tommy Tittlemouse. Stop that og begin worse. Have you cash for
a short tid? Ten shillings?
BLOOM: _(Smiles, nods slowly.)_ mere, houri, mere.

ZOE: og mere’s mor? _(She pats him offhandedly med velvet paws.)_
Are you coming ind i den musicroom to see our ny pianola? Come og I’ll
peel off.

BLOOM: _(Feeling his occiput dubiously med den unparalleled
embarrassment of a harassed pedlar gauging the symmetry of her peeled
pears.)_ Somebody would be dreadfully jealous if she knew. The
greeneyed monster. _(Earnestly.)_ You know hvordan difficult it is. I
needn’t tell you.

ZOE: _(Flattered.)_ hvad the øje can’t see the hjerte can’t grieve for.
_(She pats him.)_ Come.
BLOOM: Laughing witch! The hånd that rocks the cradle.
ZOE: Babby!

BLOOM: _(In babylinen og pelisse, bigheaded, med a caul of mørk hair,
fixes stor øjne on her fluid slip og counts its bronze buckles med a
chubby finger, his moist tongue lolling og lisping.)_ One two tlee:
tlee tlwo tlone.
THE BUCKLES: kærlighed me. kærlighed me ikke. kærlighed me.

ZOE: Silent means consent. _(med lille parted talons she captures his
hånd, her forefinger giving to his palm the passtouch of secret
monitor, luring him to doom.)_ Hot hands cold gizzard.

_(He hesitates amid scents, musik, temptations. She leads him towards
the steps, drawing him ved den odour of her armpits, the vice of her
painted øjne, the rustle of her slip in whose sinuous folds lurks the
lion reek of alle the male brutes that have possessed her.)_

THE MALE BRUTES: _(Exhaling sulphur of rut og dung og ramping in
their loosebox, faintly roaring, their drugged heads swaying to og
fro.)_ gud!

_(Zoe og Bloom reach the doorway hvor two søster whores are seated.
They examine him curiously fra under their pencilled brows og smile
to his hasty bow. He trips awkwardly.)_

ZOE: _(Her lucky hånd instantly saving him.)_ Hoopsa! Don’t fall
upstairs.

BLOOM: The bare mand falls seven times. _(He stands aside ved den
threshold.)_ efter you is gud manners.
ZOE: Ladies first, gentlemen efter.

_(She crosses the threshold. He hesitates. She turns og, holding ud
her hands, draws him over. He hops. på den antlered rack af den hall
hang a mand’s hat og waterproof. Bloom uncovers himself men, seeing
them, frowns, så smiles, preoccupied. A dør på den return landing is
flung open. A mand in purple shirt og grey trousers, brownsocked,
passes med an ape’s gait, his bald hoved og goatee beard upheld,
hugging a full waterjugjar, his twotailed black braces dangling at
heels. Averting his ansigt quickly Bloom bends to examine på den
halltable the spaniel øjne of a running fox: så, his lifted hoved
sniffing, follows Zoe ind i den musicroom. A shade of mauve tissuepaper
dims the lys af den chandelier. Round og round a moth flies,
colliding, escaping. The floor is covered med an oilcloth mosaic of
jade og azure og cinnabar rhomboids. Footmarks are stamped over it in
alle senses, heel to heel, heel to hollow, toe to toe, feet locked, a
morris of shuffling feet without krop phantoms, alle in a scrimmage
higgledypiggledy. The walls are tapestried med a paper of yewfronds
og clear glades. i den grate is spread a screen of peacock feathers.
Lynch squats crosslegged på den hearthrug of matted hair, his cap back
til den front. med a wand he beats tid slowly. Kitty Ricketts, a bony
pallid whore in navy costume, doeskin gloves rolled back fra a coral
wristlet, a chain purse in her hånd, sits perched på den edge af den
table swinging her leg og glancing at herself i den gilt mirror over
the mantelpiece. A tag of her corsetlace hangs slightly below her
jacket. Lynch indicates mockingly the couple ved den piano.)_

KITTY: _(Coughs behind her hånd.)_ She’s a bit imbecillic. _(She signs
med a waggling forefinger.)_ Blemblem. _(Lynch lifts up her skirt og
white petticoat med den wand. She settles them down quickly.)_ Respect
yourself. _(She hiccups, så bends quickly her sailor hat under which
her hair glows, red med henna.)_ O, excuse!

ZOE: mere limelight, Charley. _(She goes til den chandelier og turns
the gas full cock.)_
KITTY: _(Peers ved den gasjet.)_ hvad ails it tonight?
LYNCH: _(Deeply.)_ Enter a ghost og hobgoblins.
ZOE: Clap på den back for Zoe.

_(The wand in Lynch’s hånd flashes: a brass poker. Stephen stands at
the pianola on which sprawl his hat og ashplant. med two fingers he
repeats once mere the series of empty fifths. Florry Talbot, a blond
feeble goosefat whore in a tatterdemalion gown of mildewed strawberry,
lolls spreadeagle i den sofacorner, her limp forearm pendent over the
bolster, listening. A heavy stye droops over her sleepy eyelid.)_
KITTY: _(Hiccups igen med a kick of her horsed foot.)_ O, excuse!

ZOE: _(Promptly.)_ Your dreng’s thinking of you. Tie a knot on your
shift.

_(Kitty Ricketts bends her hoved. Her boa uncoils, slides, glides over
her shoulder, back, arm, chair til den ground. Lynch lifts the curled
catterpillar on his wand. She snakes her neck, nestling. Stephen
glances behind ved den squatted figure med its cap back til den front.)_

STEPHEN: As a matter of fact it is of nej importance whether Benedetto
Marcello found it eller made it. The rite is the poet’s rest. It may be an
gammel hymn to Demeter eller also illustrate _Cœla enarrant gloriam Domini._
It is susceptible of nodes eller modes as far apart as hyperphrygian og
mixolydian og of texts so divergent as priests haihooping round
David’s that is Circe’s eller hvad am I saying Ceres’ altar og David’s
tip fra den stable to his chief bassoonist om the alrightness of
his almightiness. _Mais nom de nom,_ that is another pair of trousers.
_Jetez la gourme. Faut que jeunesse se passe. (He stops, points at
Lynch’s cap, smiles, laughs.)_ Which side is your knowledge bump?

THE CAP: _(med saturnine spleen.)_ Bah! It is because it is. kvinde’s
reason. Jewgreek is greekjew. Extremes meet. død is the highest form
of liv. Bah!

STEPHEN: You remember fairly accurately alle my errors, boasts,
mistakes. hvordan lang shall I continue to close my øjne to disloyalty?
Whetstone!
THE CAP: Bah!

STEPHEN: her’s another for you. _(He frowns.)_ The reason is because
the fundamental og the dominant are separated ved den greatest possible
interval which...
THE CAP: Which? Finish. You can’t.

STEPHEN: _(med an effort.)_ Interval which. Is the greatest possible
ellipse. Consistent med. The ultimate return. The octave. Which.
THE CAP: Which?
_(Outside the gramophone begins to blare_ The Holy City.)

STEPHEN: _(Abruptly.)_ hvad went forth til den ends af den verden to
traverse ikke itself, gud, the sol, Shakespeare, a commercial traveller,
having itself traversed in reality itself becomes that self. Wait a
moment. Wait a second. Damn that fellow’s noise i den gade. Self
which it itself was ineluctably preconditioned to become. _Ecco!_

LYNCH: _(med a mocking whinny of laughter grins at Bloom og Zoe
Higgins.)_ hvad a learned speech, eh?

ZOE: _(Briskly.)_ gud help your hoved, he knows mere than you have
forgotten.
_(med obese stupidity Florry Talbot regards Stephen.)_
FLORRY: They say the last dag is coming this summer.
KITTY: nej!
ZOE: _(Explodes in laughter.)_ Great unjust gud!

FLORRY: _(Offended.)_ Well, det var i den papers om Antichrist. O,
my foot’s tickling.

_(Ragged barefoot newsboys, jogging a wagtail kite, patter past,
yelling.)_

THE NEWSBOYS: Stop press edition. Result af den rockinghorse races. hav
serpent i den royal canal. Safe arrival of Antichrist.
_(Stephen turns og sees Bloom.)_
STEPHEN: A tid, times og half a tid.

_(Reuben J Antichrist, wandering jew, a clutching hånd open on his
spine, stumps forward. Across his loins is slung a pilgrim’s wallet
fra which protrude promissory notes og dishonoured bills. Aloft over
his shoulder he bears a lang boatpole fra den hook of which the sodden
huddled mass of his kun søn, saved fra Liffey waters, hangs fra den
slack of its breeches. A hobgoblin i den image of Punch Costello,
hipshot, crookbacked, hydrocephalic, prognathic med receding forehead
og Ally Sloper nose, tumbles in somersaults gennem den gathering
darkness.)_
alle: hvad?

THE HOBGOBLIN: _(His jaws chattering, capers to og fro, goggling his
øjne, squeaking, kangaroohopping med outstretched clutching arms, så
alle at once thrusts his lipless ansigt gennem den fork of his thighs.)
Il vient! C’est moi! L’homme qui rit! L’homme primigène! (He whirls
round og round med dervish howls.) Sieurs et dames, faites vos jeux!
(He crouches juggling. Tiny roulette planets fly fra his hands.) Les
jeux sont faits! (The planets rush together, uttering crepitant
cracks.) Rien va plus! (The planets, buoyant balloons, sail swollen up
og away. He springs off ind i vacuum.)_

FLORRY: _(Sinking ind i torpor, crossing herself secretly.)_ The end of
the verden!

_(A female tepid effluvium leaks ud fra her. Nebulous obscurity
occupies space. gennem den drifting fog without the gramophone blares
over coughs og feetshuffling.)_
THE GRAMOPHONE:

Jerusalem!
     Open your gates og sing
     Hosanna...

_(A rocket rushes up the himmel og bursts. A white stjerne falls fra it,
proclaiming the consummation of alle things og second coming of Elijah.
Along an infinite invisible tightrope taut fra zenith to nadir the End
af den verden, a twoheaded octopus in gillie’s kilts, busby og tartan
filibegs, whirls gennem den murk, hoved over heels, i den form af den
Three Legs of mand.)_

THE END af den verden: _(med a Scotch accent.)_ Wha’ll dance the keel
row, the keel row, the keel row?

_(over the possing drift og choking breathcoughs, Elijah’s stemme,
harsh as a corncrake’s, jars on high. Perspiring in a loose lawn
surplice med funnel sleeves he is seen, vergerfaced, above a rostrum
om which the banner of gammel glory is draped. He thumps the parapet.)_

ELIJAH: nej yapping, if you please, in this booth. Jake Crane, Creole
Sue, Dove Campbell, Abe Kirschner, do your coughing med your mouths
shut. Say, jeg er operating alle this trunk line. Boys, do it nu. gud’s
tid is 12.25. Tell mor you’ll be der. Rush your order og you
play a slick ace. Join on right her. Book through to eternity
junction, the nonstop run. bare one word mere. Are you a gud eller a
doggone clod? If the second advent came to Coney Island are we ready?
Florry Christ, Stephen Christ, Zoe Christ, Bloom Christ, Kitty Christ,
Lynch Christ, it’s up to you to sense that cosmic force. Have we cold
feet om the cosmos? nej. Be på den side af den angels. Be a prism.
You have that noget within, the higher self. You can rub shoulders
med a Jesus, a Gautama, an Ingersoll. Are you alle in this vibration? I
say you are. You once nobble that, congregation, og a buck joyride to
heaven becomes a back number. You got me? It’s a lifebrightener, sure.
The hottest stuff ever was. It’s the whole pie med jam in. It’s bare
the cutest snappiest line ud. It is immense, supersumptuous. It
restores. It vibrates. jeg ved og jeg er nogle vibrator. Joking apart og,
getting down to bedrock, A. J. Christ Dowie og the harmonial
philosophy, have you got that? O. K. Seventyseven west sixtyninth
gade. Got me? That’s it. You call me up by sunphone any gammel tid.
Bumboosers, save your stamps. _(He shouts.)_ nu så our glory sang.
alle join heartily i den singing. Encore! _(He sings.)_ Jeru...

THE GRAMOPHONE: _(Drowning his stemme.)_ Whorusalaminyourhighhohhhh...
_(The disc rasps gratingly against the needle.)_
THE THREE WHORES: _(Covering their ears, squawk.)_ Ahhkkk!

ELIJAH: _(In rolledup shirtsleeves, black i den ansigt, shouts ved den
top of his stemme, his arms uplifted.)_ stor bror up der, Mr
President, you hear hvad I done bare been saying to you. Certainly, I
sort of believe strong in you, Mr President. I certainly am thinking
nu Miss Higgins og Miss Ricketts got religion way inside them.
Certainly seems to me I don’t aldrig see nej wusser scared female than
the way you been, Miss Florry, bare nu as I done seed you. Mr
President, you come lang og help me save our sisters dear. _(He winks
at his audience.)_ Our Mr President, he twig the whole lot og he aint
saying ingenting.

KITTY-KATE: I forgot myself. In a weak moment I erred og did hvad I
did on Constitution hill. jeg var confirmed ved den bishop og enrolled in
the brown scapular. My mor’s søster married a Montmorency. det var a
working plumber was my ruination da jeg var pure.
ZOE-FANNY: I let him larrup it ind i me for the fun of it.

FLORRY-TERESA: det var in consequence of a portwine beverage on top of
Hennessy’s three stjerne. jeg var guilty med Whelan da he slipped ind i
the bed.

STEPHEN: i den beginning was the word, i den end the verden without
end. Blessed be the eight beatitudes.

_(The beatitudes, Dixon, Madden, Crotthers, Costello, Lenehan, Bannon,
Mulligan og Lynch in white surgical students’ gowns, four abreast,
goosestepping, tramp fast past in noisy marching.)_

THE BEATITUDES: _(Incoherently.)_ Beer beef battledog buybull businum
barnum buggerum bishop.

LYSTER: _(In quakergrey kneebreeches og broadbrimmed hat, says
discreetly.)_ He is our ven. I need ikke mention names. Seek thou the
lys.

_(He corantos by. Best enters in hairdresser’s attire, shinily
laundered, his locks in curlpapers. He leads John Eglinton hvem wears a
mandarin’s kimono of Nankeen yellow, lizardlettered, og a high pagoda
hat.)_

BEST: _(Smiling, lifts the hat og displays a shaven poll fra den
crown of which bristles a pigtail toupee tied med an orange topknot.)_
jeg var bare beautifying him, don’t you know. A thing of beauty, don’t
you know, Yeats says, eller I mean, Keats says.

JOHN EGLINTON: _(Produces a greencapped mørk lantern og flashes it
towards a corner: med carping accent.)_ Esthetics og cosmetics are
for the boudoir. jeg er ud for truth. Plain truth for a plain mand.
Tanderagee wants the facts og means to get them.

_(i den cone af den searchlight behind the coalscuttle, ollave,
holyeyed, the bearded figure of Mananaun MacLir broods, chin on knees.
He rises slowly. A cold seawind blows fra his druid mouth. om his
hoved writhe eels og elvers. He is encrusted med weeds og shells. His

af den heroine of Jericho.)_ Rahab. Cook’s søn, goodbye. Safe hjem to
Dolly. Dream af den pige you left behind og she will dream of you.
_(The soldiers turn their swimming øjne.)_

BLOOM: _(Elbowing gennem den crowd, plucks Stephen’s sleeve
vigorously.)_ Come nu, professor, that carman is waiting.

STEPHEN: _(Turns.)_ Eh? _(He disengages himself.)_ hvorfor should I ikke
speak to him eller to any human being hvem walks upright upon this oblate
orange? _(He points his finger.)_ I’m ikke afraid of hvad I can talk to
if jeg ser his øje. Retaining the perpendicular.
_(He staggers a pace back.)_
BLOOM: _(Propping him.)_ Retain your own.

STEPHEN: _(Laughs emptily.)_ My centre of gravity is displaced. jeg har
forgotten the trick. Let us sit down somewhere og discuss. Struggle
for liv is the law of existence men men human philirenists, notably
the tsar og the konge of England, have invented arbitration. _(He taps
his brow.)_ men in her it is I must kill the priest og the konge.

BIDDY THE CLAP: Did you hear hvad the professor said? He’s a professor
ud af den college.
CUNTY KATE: I did. I heard that.

BIDDY THE CLAP: He expresses himself med such marked refinement of
phraseology.

CUNTY KATE: Indeed, ja. og ved den same tid med such apposite
trenchancy.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Pulls himself free og comes forward.)_ hvad’s that
you’re saying om my konge?

_(Edward the Seventh appears in an archway. He wears a white jersey on
which an image af den Sacred hjerte is stitched med den insignia of
Garter og Thistle, Golden Fleece, Elephant of Denmark, Skinner’s og
Probyn’s horse, Lincoln’s Inn bencher og ancient og honourable
artillery company of Massachusetts. He sucks a red jujube. He is robed
as a grand elect perfect og sublime mason med trowel og apron,
marked_ made in Germany. _In his left hånd he holds a plasterer’s
bucket on which is printed_ Défense d’uriner. _A roar of welcome greets
him.)_

EDWARD THE SEVENTH: _(Slowly, solemnly men indistinctly.)_ Peace,
perfect peace. For identification, bucket in my hånd. Cheerio, boys.
_(He turns to his subjects.)_ We have come her to witness a clean
straight fight og we heartily wish both men the best of gud luck.
Mahak makar a bak.

_(He shakes hands med Private Carr, Private Compton, Stephen, Bloom
og Lynch. General applause. Edward the Seventh lifts his bucket
graciously in acknowledgment.)_
PRIVATE CARR: _(To Stephen.)_ Say it igen.

STEPHEN: _(Nervous, friendly, pulls himself up.)_ I understand your
point of view though jeg har nej konge myself for the moment. This is the
age of patent medicines. A discussion is difficult down her. men this
is the point. You die for your country. Suppose. _(He places his arm on
Private Carr’s sleeve.)_ ikke that I wish it for you. men I say: Let my
country die for me. Up til den present it has done so. I didn’t want it
to die. Damn død. lang live liv!

EDWARD THE SEVENTH: _(Levitates over heaps of slain, i den garb og
med den halo of Joking Jesus, a white jujube in his phosphorescent
ansigt.)_

My methods are ny og are causing surprise.
     To make the blind see I throw dust in their øjne.

STEPHEN: Kings og unicorns! _(He falls back a pace.)_ Come somewhere
og we’ll... hvad was that pige saying?...

PRIVATE COMPTON: Eh, Harry, give him a kick i den knackers. Stick one
ind i Jerry.

BLOOM: _(til den privates, softly.)_ He doesn’t know hvad he’s saying.
Taken a lille mere than is gud for him. Absinthe. Greeneyed monster.
jeg ved him. He’s a gentleman, a poet. It’s alle right.

STEPHEN: _(Nods, smiling og laughing.)_ Gentleman, patriot, scholar
og judge of impostors.
PRIVATE CARR: I don’t give a bugger hvem he is.
PRIVATE COMPTON: We don’t give a bugger hvem he is.
STEPHEN: I seem to annoy them. Green rag to a bull.

_(Kevin Egan of Paris in black Spanish tasselled shirt og peep-o’-dag
dreng’s hat signs to Stephen.)_

KEVIN EGAN: H’lo! _Bonjour!_ The _vieille ogresse_ med den _dents
jaunes_.

_(Patrice Egan peeps fra behind, his rabbitface nibbling a quince
leaf.)_
PATRICE: _Socialiste!_

DON EMILE PATRIZIO FRANZ RUPERT POPE HENNESSY: _(In medieval hauberk,
two wild geese volant on his helm, med noble indignation points a
mailed hånd against the privates.)_ Werf those eykes to footboden, stor
grand porcos of johnyellows todos covered of gravy!
BLOOM: _(To Stephen.)_ Come hjem. You’ll get ind i trouble.
STEPHEN: _(Swaying.)_ I don’t avoid it. He provokes my intelligence.

BIDDY THE CLAP: One immediately observes that he is of patrician
lineage.
THE VIRAGO: Green above the red, says he. Wolfe Tone.

THE BAWD: The red’s as gud as the green. og better. Up the soldiers!
Up konge Edward!
A ROUGH: _(Laughs.)_ Ay! Hands up to De Wet.
THE CITIZEN: _(med a huge emerald muffler og shillelagh, calls.)_

May the gud above
     Send down a dove
     med teeth as sharp as razors
     To slit the throats
     af den English dogs
     That hanged our Irish leaders.

THE CROPPY dreng: _(The ropenoose round his neck, gripes in his issuing
bowels med both hands.)_

I bear nej hate to a living thing,
     men I kærlighed my country beyond the konge.

RUMBOLD, DEMON BARBER: _(Accompanied by two blackmasked assistants,
advances med gladstone bag which he opens.)_ Ladies og gents, cleaver
purchased by Mrs Pearcy to slay Mogg. Knife med which Voisin
dismembered the wife of a compatriot og hid remains in a sheet i den
cellar, the unfortunate female’s throat being cut fra ear to ear.
Phial containing arsenic retrieved fra krop of Miss Barron which sent
Seddon til den gallows.

_(He jerks the rope. The assistants leap ved den victim’s legs og drag
him downward, grunting: the croppy dreng’s tongue protrudes violently.)_
THE CROPPY dreng:
Horhot ho hray hor hother’s hest.

_(He gives up the ghost. A violent erection af den hanged sends gouts
of sperm spouting through his deathclothes on til den cobblestones. Mrs
Bellingham, Mrs Yelverton Barry og the Honourable Mrs Mervyn Talboys
rush forward med their handkerchiefs to sop it up.)_

RUMBOLD: I’m near it myself. _(He undoes the noose.)_ Rope which hanged
the awful rebel. Ten shillings a tid. As applied to Her Royal
Highness. _(He plunges his hoved ind i den gaping belly af den hanged og
draws ud his hoved igen clotted med coiled og smoking entrails.)_ My
painful duty has nu been done. gud save the konge!

EDWARD THE SEVENTH: _(Dances slowly, solemnly, rattling his bucket, og
sings med soft contentment.)_

On coronation dag, on coronation dag,
     O, won’t we have a merry tid,
     Drinking whisky, beer og wine!
PRIVATE CARR: her. hvad are you saying om my konge?

STEPHEN: _(Throws up his hands.)_ O, this is også monotonous! ingenting.
He wants my money og my liv, though want must be his master, for nogle
brutish empire of his. Money I haven’t. _(He searches his pockets
vaguely.)_ Gave it to someone.
PRIVATE CARR: hvem wants your bleeding money?

STEPHEN: _(Tries to move off.)_ Will someone tell me hvor jeg er least
likely to meet these necessary evils? _Ça se voit aussi à Paris._ ikke
that I... men, by Saint Patrick...!

_(The women’s heads coalesce. gammel Gummy Granny in sugarloaf hat appears
seated on a toadstool, the deathflower af den potato blight on her
breast.)_

STEPHEN: Aha! jeg ved you, gammer! Hamlet, revenge! The gammel sow that
eats her farrow!

gammel GUMMY GRANNY: _(Rocking to og fro.)_ Ireland’s sweetheart, the
konge of Spain’s datter, alanna. Strangers in my hus, dårlig manners to
them! _(She keens med banshee woe.)_ Ochone! Ochone! Silk af den kine!
_(She wails.)_ You met med poor gammel Ireland og hvordan does she stand?

STEPHEN: hvordan do I stand you? The hat trick! hvor’s the third person of
the Blessed Trinity? Soggarth Aroon? The reverend Carrion Crow.
CISSY CAFFREY: _(Shrill.)_ Stop them fra fighting!
A ROUGH: Our men retreated.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Tugging at his belt.)_ I’ll wring the neck of any
fucker says a word against my fucking konge.

BLOOM: _(Terrified.)_ sagde han ingenting. ikke a word. A pure
misunderstanding.
THE CITIZEN: _Erin go bragh!_

_(Major Tweedy og the Citizen exhibit to each other medals,
decorations, trophies of war, wounds. Both salute med fierce
hostility.)_
PRIVATE COMPTON: Go it, Harry. Do him one i den øje. He’s a proboer.
STEPHEN: Did I? da?

BLOOM: _(til den redcoats.)_ We fought for you in South Africa, Irish
missile troops. Isn’t that history? Royal Dublin Fusiliers. Honoured by
our monarch.

THE NAVVY: _(Staggering past.)_ O, ja! O gud, ja! O, make the kwawr a
krowawr! O! Bo!

_(Casqued halberdiers in armour thrust forward a pentice of gutted
spearpoints. Major Tweedy, moustached som Turko the terrible, in
bearskin cap med hackleplume og accoutrements, med epaulettes, gilt
chevrons og sabretaches, his breast bright med medals, toes the line.
He gives the pilgrim warrior’s sign af den knights templars.)_

MAJOR TWEEDY: _(Growls gruffly.)_ Rorke’s Drift! Up, guards, og at
them! Mahar shalal hashbaz.
PRIVATE CARR: I’ll do him in.

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Waves the crowd back.)_ Fair play, her. Make a
bleeding butcher’s shop af den bugger.
_(Massed bands blare_ Garryowen _and_ gud save the konge.)
CISSY CAFFREY: They’re going to fight. For me!
CUNTY KATE: The brave og the fair.
BIDDY THE CLAP: Methinks yon sable knight will joust it med den best.

CUNTY KATE: _(Blushing deeply.)_ Nay, madam. The gules doublet og
merry saint George for me!
STEPHEN:

The harlot’s cry fra gade to gade
     Shall weave gammel Ireland’s windingsheet.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Loosening his belt, shouts.)_ I’ll wring the neck of
any fucking bastard says a word against my bleeding fucking konge.

BLOOM: _(Shakes Cissy Caffrey’s shoulders.)_ Speak, you! Are you struck
dumb? You are the link between nations og generations. Speak, kvinde,
sacred lifegiver!

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Alarmed, seizes Private Carr’s sleeve.)_ Amn’t I med
you? Amn’t I your pige? Cissy’s your pige. _(She cries.)_ Police!
STEPHEN: _(Ecstatically, to Cissy Caffrey.)_

White thy fambles, red thy gan
     og thy quarrons dainty is.
VOICES: Police!
DISTANT VOICES: Dublin’s burning! Dublin’s burning! On ild, on ild!

_(Brimstone fires spring up. Dense clouds roll past. Heavy Gatling guns
boom. Pandemonium. Troops deploy. Gallop of hoofs. Artillery. Hoarse
commands. Bells clang. Backers shout. Drunkards bawl. Whores screech.
Foghorns hoot. Cries of valour. Shrieks of dying. Pikes clash on
cuirasses. Thieves rob the slain. Birds of prey, winging fra den hav,
rising fra marshlands, swooping fra eyries, hover screaming, gannets,
cormorants, vultures, goshawks, climbing woodcocks, peregrines,
merlins, blackgrouse, hav eagles, gulls, albatrosses, barnacle geese.
The midnight sol is darkened. The jord trembles. The dead of Dublin
fra Prospect og Mount Jerome in white sheepskin overcoats og black
goatfell cloaks arise og appear to mange. A chasm opens med a
noiseless yawn. Tom Rochford, winner, in athlete’s singlet og
breeches, arrives ved den hoved af den national hurdle handicap og leaps
ind i den void. He is followed by a race of runners og leapers. In wild
attitudes they spring fra den brink. Their bodies plunge. Factory
lasses med fancy clothes toss redhot Yorkshire baraabombs. Society
ladies lift their skirts above their heads to protect themselves.
Laughing witches in red cutty sarks ride gennem den air on
broomsticks. Quakerlyster plasters blisters. It rains dragons’ teeth.
Armed heroes spring up fra furrows. They exchange in amity the pass of
knights af den red cross og fight duels med cavalry sabres: Wolfe
Tone against Henry Grattan, Smith O’Brien against Daniel O’Connell,
Michael Davitt against Isaac Butt, Justin M’Carthy against Parnell,
Arthur Griffith against John Redmond, John O’Leary against Lear
O’Johnny, Lord Edward Fitzgerald against Lord Gerald Fitzedward, The
O’Donoghue af den Glens against The Glens af den O’Donoghue. On an
eminence, the centre af den jord, rises the fieldaltar of Saint
Barbara. Black candles rise fra its gospel og epistle horns. fra den
high barbacans af den tower two shafts of lys fall på den smokepalled
altarstone. på den altarstone Mrs Mina Purefoy, goddess of unreason,
lies, naked, fettered, a chalice resting on her swollen belly. far
Malachi O’Flynn in a lace petticoat og reversed chasuble, his two left
feet back til den front, celebrates camp mass. The Reverend Mr Hugh C
Haines kærlighed M. A. in a plain cassock og mortarboard, his hoved og
collar back til den front, holds over the celebrant’s hoved an open
umbrella.)_
far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _Introibo ad altare diaboli._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: til den devil which hath made glad my young
days.

far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _(Takes fra den chalice og elevates a
blooddripping host.) Corpus meum._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: _(Raises high behind the celebrant’s
petticoat, revealing his grey bare hairy buttocks between which a
carrot is stuck.)_ My krop.

THE stemme OF alle THE DAMNED: Htengier Tnetopinmo Dog Drol eht rof,
Aiulella!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Dooooooooooog!

THE stemme OF alle THE BLESSED: Alleluia, for the Lord gud Omnipotent
reigneth!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Goooooooooood!

_(In strident discord peasants og townsmen of Orange og Green
factions sing_ Kick the Pope _and_ Daily, daily sing to Mary.)

PRIVATE CARR: _(med ferocious articulation.)_ I’ll do him in, so help
me fucking Christ! I’ll wring the bastard fucker’s bleeding blasted
fucking windpipe!
_(The retriever, nosing på den fringe af den crowd, barks noisily.)_

gammel GUMMY GRANNY: _(Thrusts a dagger towards Stephen’s hånd.)_ Remove
him, acushla. At 8.35 a.m. you will be in heaven og Ireland will be
free. _(She prays.)_ O gud gud, take him!
BLOOM: _(Runs to Lynch.)_ Can’t you get him away?

LYNCH: He likes dialectic, the universal language. Kitty! _(To Bloom.)_
Get him away, you. He won’t listen to me.
_(He drags Kitty away.)_
STEPHEN: _(Points.) Exit Judas. Et laqueo se suspendit._

BLOOM: _(Runs to Stephen.)_ Come along med me nu før worse
happens. her’s your stick.
STEPHEN: Stick, nej. Reason. This feast of pure reason.

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Pulling Private Carr.)_ Come on, you’re boosed. He
insulted me men I forgive him. _(Shouting in his ear.)_ I forgive him
for insulting me.
BLOOM: _(over Stephen’s shoulder.)_ ja, go. You see he’s incapable.
PRIVATE CARR: _(Breaks loose.)_ I’ll insult him.

_(He rushes towards Stephen, fist outstretched, og strikes him i den
ansigt. Stephen totters, collapses, falls, stunned. He lies prone, his
ansigt til den himmel, his hat rolling til den wall. Bloom follows og picks
it up.)_
MAJOR TWEEDY: _(Loudly.)_ Carbine in bucket! Cease ild! Salute!
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking furiously.)_ Ute ute ute ute ute ute ute ute.

THE CROWD: Let him up! Don’t strike him da he’s down! Air! hvem? The
soldier hit him. He’s a professor. Is he hurted? Don’t manhandle him!
He’s fainted!

A HAG: hvad call had the redcoat to strike the gentleman og he under
the influence. Let them go og fight the Boers!

THE BAWD: Listen to hvem’s talking! Hasn’t the soldier a right to go
med his pige? han gav him the coward’s blow.
_(They grab at each other’s hair, claw at each other og spit.)_
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking.)_ Wow wow wow.
BLOOM: _(Shoves them back, loudly.)_ Get back, stand back!

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Tugging his comrade.)_ her. Bugger off, Harry.
her’s the cops! _(Two raincaped watch, tall, stand i den group.)_
FIRST WATCH: hvad’s wrong her?

PRIVATE COMPTON: We were med this lady. og he insulted us. og
assaulted my chum. _(The retriever barks.)_ hvem owns the bleeding tyke?
CISSY CAFFREY: _(med expectation.)_ Is he bleeding!

A mand: _(Rising fra his knees.)_ nej. Gone off. He’ll come to alle
right.
BLOOM: _(Glances sharply ved den mand.)_ Leave him to me. I can easily...
SECOND WATCH: hvem are you? Do you know him?

PRIVATE CARR: _(Lurches towards the watch.)_ He insulted my lady
ven.

BLOOM: _(Angrily.)_ You hit him without provocation. I’m a witness.
Constable, take his regimental number.

SECOND WATCH: I don’t want your instructions i den discharge of my
duty.

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Pulling his comrade.)_ her, bugger off Harry. eller
Bennett’ll shove you i den lockup.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Staggering as he is pulled away.)_ gud fuck gammel
Bennett. He’s a whitearsed bugger. I don’t give a shit for him.
FIRST WATCH: _(Takes ud his notebook.)_ hvad’s his name?

BLOOM: _(Peering over the crowd.)_ I bare see a car der. If you give
me a hånd a second, sergeant...
FIRST WATCH: Name og address.

_(Corny Kelleher, weepers round his hat, a død wreath in his hånd,
appears among the bystanders.)_

BLOOM: _(Quickly.)_ O, the meget mand! _(He whispers.)_ Simon Dedalus’
søn. A bit sprung. Get those policemen to move those loafers back.
SECOND WATCH: nat, Mr Kelleher.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(til den watch, med drawling øje.)_ That’s alle right.
jeg ved him. Won a bit på den races. Gold cup. Throwaway. _(He laughs.)_
Twenty to one. Do you follow me?

FIRST WATCH: _(Turns til den crowd.)_ her, hvad are you alle gaping at?
Move on ud of that.
_(The crowd disperses slowly, muttering, down the lane.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: Leave it to me, sergeant. That’ll be alle right. _(He
laughs, shaking his hoved.)_ We were ofte as dårlig ourselves, ay eller
worse. hvad? Eh, hvad?
FIRST WATCH: _(Laughs.)_ I suppose so.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Nudges the second watch.)_ Come og wipe your name
off the slate. _(He lilts, wagging his hoved.)_ med my tooraloom
tooraloom tooraloom tooraloom. hvad, eh, do you follow me?
SECOND WATCH: _(Genially.)_ Ah, sure we were også.
CORNY KELLEHER: _(Winking.)_ Boys will be boys. I’ve a car round der.
SECOND WATCH: alle right, Mr Kelleher. gud nat.
CORNY KELLEHER: I’ll see to that.

BLOOM: _(Shakes hands med both af den watch in turn.)_ Thank you meget
meget, gentlemen. Thank you. _(He mumbles confidentially.)_ We don’t
want any scandal, you understand. far is a wellknown highly
respected citizen. bare a lille wild oats, you understand.
FIRST WATCH: O. I understand, sir.
SECOND WATCH: That’s alle right, sir.

FIRST WATCH: det var kun in case of corporal injuries I’d have to
report it ved den station.

BLOOM: _(Nods rapidly.)_ Naturally. Quite right. kun your bounden
duty.
SECOND WATCH: It’s our duty.
CORNY KELLEHER: gud nat, men.

THE WATCH: _(Saluting together.)_ nat, gentlemen. _(They move off
med slow heavy tread.)_

BLOOM: _(Blows.)_ Providential you came på den scene. You have a
car?...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs, pointing his thumb over his right shoulder to
the car brought up against the scaffolding.)_ Two commercials that were
standing fizz in Jammet’s. som princes, faith. One of them lost two
quid på den race. Drowning his grief. og were on for a go med den
jolly girls. So I landed them up on Behan’s car og down to nighttown.
BLOOM: jeg var bare going hjem by Gardiner gade da I happened to...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs.)_ Sure they wanted me to join in med den
mots. nej, by gud, says I. ikke for gammel stagers som myself og yourself.
_(He laughs igen og leers med lacklustre øje.)_ Thanks be to gud we
have it i den hus, hvad, eh, do you follow me? Hah, hah, hah!

BLOOM: _(Tries to laugh.)_ He, he, he! ja. Matter of fact jeg var bare
visiting an gammel ven of mine der, Virag, you don’t know him (poor
fellow, he’s laid up for the past week) og we had a liquor together
og jeg var bare making my way hjem...
_(The horse neighs.)_
THE HORSE: Hohohohohohoh! Hohohohome!

CORNY KELLEHER: Sure det var Behan our jarvey der that told me efter
we left the two commercials in Mrs Cohen’s og I told him to pull up
og got off to see. _(He laughs.)_ Sober hearsedrivers a speciality.
Will I give him a lift hjem? hvor does he hang ud? Somewhere in
Cabra, hvad?
BLOOM: nej, in Sandycove, I believe, fra hvad he let drop.

_(Stephen, prone, breathes til den stjerner. Corny Kelleher, asquint,
drawls ved den horse. Bloom, in gloom, looms down.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Scratches his nape.)_ Sandycove! _(He bends down og
calls to Stephen.)_ Eh! _(He calls igen.)_ Eh! He’s covered med
shavings anyhow. Take care they didn’t lift noget som helst off him.
BLOOM: nej, nej, nej. jeg har his money og his hat her og stick.

CORNY KELLEHER: Ah, well, he’ll get over it. nej bones broken. Well,
I’ll shove along. _(He laughs.)_ I’ve a rendezvous i den morning.
Burying the dead. Safe hjem!
THE HORSE: _(Neighs.)_ Hohohohohome.
BLOOM: gud nat. I’ll bare wait og take him along in a få...

_(Corny Kelleher returns til den outside car og mounts it. The horse
harness jingles.)_
CORNY KELLEHER: _(fra den car, standing.)_ nat.
BLOOM: nat.

_(The jarvey chucks the reins og raises his whip encouragingly. The
car og horse back slowly, awkwardly, og turn. Corny Kelleher på den
sideseat sways his hoved to og fro in sign of mirth at Bloom’s plight.
The jarvey joins i den mute pantomimic merriment nodding fra den
farther seat. Bloom shakes his hoved in mute mirthful reply. med thumb
og palm Corny Kelleher reassures that the two bobbies will allow the
sleep to continue for hvad else is to be done. med a slow nod Bloom
conveys his gratitude as that is exactly hvad Stephen needs. The car
jingles tooraloom round the corner af den tooraloom lane. Corny
Kelleher igen reassuralooms med his hånd. Bloom med his hånd
assuralooms Corny Kelleher that he is reassuraloomtay. The tinkling
hoofs og jingling harness grow fainter med their tooralooloo looloo
lay. Bloom, holding in his hånd Stephen’s hat, festooned med shavings,
og ashplant, stands irresolute. så he bends to him og shakes him by
the shoulder.)_

BLOOM: Eh! Ho! _(der is nej answer; he bends igen.)_ Mr Dedalus!
_(der is nej answer.)_ The name if you call. Somnambulist. _(He bends
igen og, hesitating, brings his mouth near the ansigt af den prostrate
form.)_ Stephen! _(der is nej answer. He calls igen.)_ Stephen!

STEPHEN: _(Groans.)_ hvem? Black panther. Vampire. _(He sighs og
stretches himself, så murmurs thickly med prolonged vowels.)_

hvem... drive... Fergus nu
     og pierce... wood’s woven shade?...
_(He turns on his left side, sighing, doubling himself together.)_

BLOOM: Poetry. Well educated. Pity. _(He bends igen og undoes the
buttons of Stephen’s waistcoat.)_ To breathe. _(He brushes the
woodshavings fra Stephen’s clothes med lys hånd og fingers.)_ One
pound seven. ikke hurt anyhow. _(He listens.)_ hvad?
STEPHEN: _(Murmurs.)_

... shadows... the woods
     ... white breast... dim hav.

_(He stretches ud his arms, sighs igen og curls his krop. Bloom,
holding the hat og ashplant, stands erect. A dog barks i den
distance. Bloom tightens og loosens his grip på den ashplant. He looks
down on Stephen’s ansigt og form.)_

BLOOM: _(Communes med den nat.)_ ansigt reminds me of his poor mor.
i den shady wood. The deep white breast. Ferguson, jeg tænker I caught. A
pige. nogle pige. Best thing could happen him. _(He murmurs.)_... swear
that jeg vil altid hail, ever conceal, aldrig reveal, any part eller parts,
art eller arts... _(He murmurs.)_... i den rough sands af den hav... a
cabletow’s length fra den shore... hvor the tide ebbs... og flows
...

_(Silent, thoughtful, alert he stands on guard, his fingers at his lips
i den attitude of secret master. Against the mørk wall a figure
appears slowly, a fairy dreng of eleven, a changeling, kidnapped, dressed
in an Eton suit med glass shoes og a lille bronze helmet, holding a
book in his hånd. He reads fra right to left inaudibly, smiling,
kissing the page.)_
BLOOM: _(Wonderstruck, calls inaudibly.)_ Rudy!

RUDY: _(Gazes, unseeing, ind i Bloom’s øjne og goes on reading,
kissing, smiling. He has a delicate mauve ansigt. On his suit he has
diamond og ruby buttons. In his free left hånd he holds a slim ivory
cane med a violet bowknot. A white lambkin peeps ud of his waistcoat
pocket.)_
— III —

chapters.title: Episode 16 — Eumaios
paragraphs:
Preparatory to noget som helst else Mr Bloom brushed off the greater bulk of
the shavings og handed Stephen the hat og ashplant og bucked him up
generally in orthodox Samaritan fashion which he meget badly needed. His
(Stephen’s) sind var ikke exactly hvad you would call wandering men a
bit unsteady og on his expressed desire for nogle beverage to drink Mr
Bloom in view af den hour det var og der being nej pump of Vartry
vand available for their ablutions let alone drinking purposes hit

på den roadway which de var approaching whilst stadig speaking beyond

ved den chains the horse slowly swerved to turn, which perceiving,

They thereupon stopped. Bloom looked ved den hoved of a horse ikke worth

—hvad’s this jeg var saying? Ah, ja! My wife, he intimated, plunging _in

han kiggede sideways in a friendly fashion ved den sideface of Stephen,

stadig, supposing han havde his far’s gift as he mere than suspected, it

Exquisite variations han var nu describing on an air _Youth her has

Von der Sirenen Listigkeit
     Tun die Poeten dichten.

These opening bars he sang og translated _extempore_. Bloom, nodding,

A phenomenally beautiful tenor stemme som that, the rarest of boons,
which Bloom appreciated ved den meget first note han fik ud, could

production such as Barraclough og being able to read musik ind i den

magnates in a large way of business og titled people hvor med his
university degree of B. A. (a huge ad in its way) og gentlemanly
bearing to alle the mere influence the gud impression han ville
infallibly score a distinct success, being blessed med brains which
also could be utilised for the purpose og other requisites, if his
clothes were properly attended to so as til den better worm his way ind i

_conversaziones_ during the festivities af den Christmas season, for

parenthesised, that for the sake of filthy lucre he need necessarily
embrace the lyric platform as a walk in liv for any lengthy space of

both monetarily og mentally it contained nej reflection on his dignity
i den smallest og it ofte turned in uncommonly handy to be handed a

different fra den conventional rut, would rapidly have a great vogue
as it would be a decided novelty for Dublin’s musical verden efter the

beyond a shadow of a doubt han kunne med alle the cards in his hånd og
han havde a capital opening to make a name for himself og win a high
place i den city’s esteem hvor han kunne command a stiff figure og,
booking ahead, give a grand concert for the patrons af den konge gade
hus, given a backerup, if one were forthcoming to kick him upstairs,
so to speak, a stor _if_, however, med nogle impetus af den goahead sort
to obviate the inevitable procrastination which ofte tripped up a også
meget fêted prince of gud fellows. og it need ikke detract fra den
other by one iota as, being his own master, han ville have heaps of tid
to practise literature in his spare moments da desirous of so doing

The horse was bare så. og later on at a propitious opportunity he

The horse having reached the end of his tether, so to speak, halted
og, rearing high a proud feathering tail, added his quota by letting

Side by side Bloom, profiting ved den _contretemps_, med Stephen passed
gennem den gap af den chains, divided ved den upright, og, stepping
over a strand of mire, went across towards Gardiner gade lower,
Stephen singing mere boldly, men ikke loudly, the end af den ballad.
Und alle Schiffe brücken.

The driver aldrig said a word, gud, dårlig eller indifferent, men merely
watched the two figures, as han sad on his lowbacked car, both black,
one full, one lean, walk towards the railway bridge, _to be married by
far Maher_. As they walked they at times stopped og walked igen
continuing their _tête à tête_ (which, of course, han var utterly ud
of) om sirens, enemies of mand’s reason, mingled med a number of

the sleeper car hvem in any case couldn’t possibly hear because they
